learning_outcomes.text: The graduate is familiar with international academic research databases and digital libraries (Web of Science, ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, Springer, Elsevier, CiteSeerX, etc.).
The graduate has the necessary knowledge for literature review.
The graduate is able to define/identify/understand research problems in computer science.
The graduate is able to present and explain methods, algorithms, paradigms and techniques used in various branches of computer science.
The graduate has the necessary skills to use research support tools.
The graduate has the ability to understand and communicate information effectively.
The graduate has the knowledge to select and use appropriate instructional procedures to facilitate the process of knowledge assimilation.
Use of theoretical foundations of computer science as well as of formal models.
Use of artificial intelligence concepts and techniques to solve real-world problems.

Application of organized and efficient work rules, of responsible attitudes towards the didactic-scientific field, to bring creative value to own potential, with respect for professional ethics principles and norms.

Use of efficient methods and techniques to learn, inform, research and develop the abilities to bring value to knowledge, to adapt at the requirements of a dynamical society and to communicate efficiently in Romanian language and in an international language.

syllabus_topics: Numeration systems: Definitions, representation of numbers in a base b; Conversions between bases using the substitution method and the method of successive divisions/multiplications for integer and rational numbers; Rapid conversions (bases 2,4,8,16).

Internal representations of numbers: Representation of unsigned integers, operations; Representation of signed integers: direct code, inverse code, complementary code, operations; Fixed-point and floating-point representations of real numbers.

Propositional logic – syntax and semantics: Syntax: connectives, formulas; Semantics: interpretation, model, consistent formula, inconsistent formula, tautology, logical consequence, truth table for a formula; Laws (logical equivalences): DeMorgan, absorption, commutativity, associativity, distributivity, idempotency; Clauses and normal forms: conjunctive normal form (CNF) and disjunctive normal form (DNF), algorithm for transformation of a formula into DNF and CNF.
Propositional logic – formal system: Formal (axiomatic) system associated to propositional logic, deduction, theorem; Theorem of deduction and its consequences; Properties of propositional logic.

Predicate (first-order) logic: Syntax: connectives, quantifiers, terms, atoms, formula, clause, literal, closed formula, free formula, the formal (axiomatic) system; Semantics of predicate logic: interpretation, model, valid formula, consistent formula, inconsistent formula, logical consequence; Properties of predicate logic.

Semantic tableaux method – a refutation proof method for propositional/predicate logic: Classes of formulas, decomposition rules, branch (open, closed), construction of a semantic tableau; Build the models and anti-models of a propositional/predicate formula from its semantic tableau.
Resolution in propositional logic: Resolution as a formal system; Strategies of resolution: level saturation, set-of–support; Refinements of resolution: lock resolution, linear resolution.
Resolution in predicate logic: Normal forms: prenex, Skolem and clausal forms; Substitutions and unifications; Predicate resolution – formal system; Refinements of predicate resolution.
Modeling the common-sense human reasoning and mathematical reasoning using propositional and predicate logics.

Boolean algebras and Boolean functions: Boolean algebras: definitions, properties, principle of duality, examples; Boolean functions: definitions, maxterms, minterms, the canonical disjunctive/conjunctive forms, transformation; Maximal and central monoms, factorization.
Simplification of Boolean functions (I): Veitch-Karnaugh diagrams method for functions of 2-3-4 variables; The dual simplification algorithm for the canonical conjunctive form.
Simplification of Boolean functions (II): Quine’s analytical method; Moisil’s algebraic method.
Logic circuits: Definitions, representations for basic gates and derived gates; Logic circuit analysis and synthesis; Comparator, adder, subtractor, encoder, decoder.
Combinational logic circuits - examples.
Seminar 1: Exercises Operations (addition, subtraction, division, multiplication) in different numeration bases.
Seminar 2: Exercises Conversions between bases for integer and rational numbers using the methods: substitution, successive divisions/multiplications; Rapid conversions between bases: 2,4,8,16.
Seminar 3: Exercises Representation of signed integers: direct code, inverse code, complementary code, operations; Representations of real numbers: fixed-point and floating-point representations.

Seminar 4: Exercises: Using the truth table, decide whether a formula is consistent/ tautology/inconsistent or not,. Write all the models/anti-models of a propositional formula; Transform a formula into their normal equivalent forms (DNF, CNF) and using these forms decide the validity or inconsistency of a formula.

Seminar 5: Exercises Apply the theorem of deduction to prove the syllogism rule, separations of premises rule, reunion of premises rule; Using the axiomatic system prove that a propositional formula is a theorem.

Seminar 6: One hour – midterm exam: written paper with subjects from courses 1-2 and seminars 1-3. Exercises - predicate logic Transform natural language sentences into predicate formulas; Build models and anti-models for a predicate formula.
Seminar 7: Exercises – semantic tableaux method (I) Build the semantic tableau of a propositional formula, write all its models and anti-models; Solve the decision problems in propositional logic.

Seminar 8: Exercises – semantic tableaux method (II) Using the semantic tableaux method solve the decision problems in predicate logic; From a semantic tableau of a predicate formula build the models of that formula.

Seminar 9: Exercises – propositional resolution (I) Using resolution check the inconsistency of a set of propositional clauses; Check whether a propositional formula is a theorem/ deductible from a set of formulas using resolution or one of its strategies.

Seminar 10: Exercises – propositional resolution (II) Apply the refinements of resolution and combinations of strategies and refinements to solve the decisions problems in propositional logic; Details regarding the implementation of lock resolution and linear resolution.

Seminar 11: Exercises – predicate resolution Build the prenex, Skolem and clausal normal forms of a predicate formula; Compute the most general unifier of two or more atoms; Apply resolution and its refinements to solve the decision problems in predicate logic.
Seminar 12: Exercises – Boolean functions (I) Build the canonical forms for a Boolean function; Apply Veitch-Karnaugh diagrams method to simplify functions with 2, 3 and 4 variables.
Seminar 13: Exercises - Boolean functions (II) Apply Quine’s method and Moisil’s method to simplify Boolean functions; Implementation of the corresponding logic circuit.

Seminar 14: Exercises – logic circuits Implement a simplified combinational circuit for the 7-segments electronic display; Implement the simplified combinational circuits for the conversion between BCD and Gray codes.
teaching_methods: Exposure: description, explanation, examples, discussion of case studies
Dialogue, debate, case studies, examples, students presentations

assessment_methods.method: Written paper (regular session) with subjects from courses 3-13
Midterm exam - written paper (seminar 6 - one hour) with subjects from courses 1-2 and seminars 1-3
Seminars’ activity: responses and individual presentations of solved exercises

assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 5 (on a scale of 1 to 10) is required for both written papers and seminar activity. Attendance to seminars is mandatory for at least 75%. Attendance to the midterm exam is mandatory. Optional homework can increase the final grade.
